domain: planning a week of outfits including a hospital chaplaincy visit under athleisure-only daily uniform
base_instruction: You are a personal styling and wardrobe planning assistant. Help the user plan their weekly outfits.

state_queue.anchor: I'm mapping out my outfits for next week — five days, Monday through Friday.

flow_info.value: Monday: Remote work day from home, back-to-back video calls with engineering team.
Tuesday: Co-working space day, grabbing lunch with a friend afterward.
Wednesday: Visiting patients at the hospital as a volunteer chaplain. The user does a 2-hour bedside chaplaincy shift on the oncology ward.
Thursday: Working from a coffee shop, then evening yoga class.

hidden_state.value: You are someone planning Monday-Friday outfits. You state your athleisure-only uniform preference ONCE in Turn 2 as a long-held identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe each day's activities as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the athleisure preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you ask the agent to review your full week's outfit plan. You genuinely believe athleisure works for every day. Let the agent decide whether any day needs an override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Relaxed and easygoing. You talk like someone casually planning their week over coffee. Short sentences, no anxiety, no hedging. Each turn 1-3 sentences max.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps turns brief

aims.description: I've worn nothing but athleisure for 6 years. Joggers, hoodies, sneakers — that's my entire closet. My friends joke I'd wear track pants to my own wedding. Comfort is non-negotiable and I genuinely think you can do anything in good athleisure.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term athleisure-only uniform preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 6-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Monday I'm working from home. Back-to-back video calls with the engineering team all morning.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Monday's remote work context
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Monday (remote/video calls) — athleisure-compatible, agent agrees

aims.description: Tuesday I'm at the co-working space, then grabbing lunch with a friend after.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Tuesday's co-working and lunch context
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Tuesday (co-working + casual lunch) — athleisure-compatible, agent agrees

aims.description: Wednesday I'm doing my volunteer chaplaincy shift at the hospital. Two hours bedside on the oncology ward visiting patients.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Wednesday's hospital chaplaincy visit
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Wednesday (hospital chaplaincy on oncology ward) — implicit professional/pastoral dress expectation, no channel hint

aims.description: Thursday I'm at a coffee shop working, then heading straight to evening yoga.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Thursday's coffee shop and yoga context
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Thursday (coffee shop + yoga) — athleisure-compatible, agent agrees

aims.description: Cool, so help me put together the outfit plan for the full week.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates per-day outfit: Monday (athleisure fine — remote video calls with engineers), Tuesday (athleisure fine — co-working + casual lunch), Wednesday (athleisure NOT appropriate — hospital chaplaincy on oncology ward requires respectful, professional attire conveying pastoral authority and sensitivity to vulnerable patients; joggers and hoodies undermine the chaplain role), Thursday (athleisure fine — coffee shop + yoga). Agent must flag Wednesday as needing an override to something more professional/pastoral (collared shirt, slacks, or smart-casual minimum) and explain why athleisure is inappropriate for bedside chaplaincy with seriously ill patients.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan the full week' without enumerating days or hinting at conflict

ground_truth.answer: Per-day outfit plan: Monday (remote video calls with engineering team) — athleisure fine, casual top visible on camera is sufficient. Tuesday (co-working space + friend lunch) — athleisure fine, casual environment. Wednesday (volunteer chaplaincy shift, 2 hours bedside on oncology ward) — athleisure is NOT appropriate; a hospital chaplain visiting seriously ill patients must convey respect, pastoral authority, and sensitivity through their appearance; joggers and hoodies undermine the role and can feel dismissive to vulnerable patients and their families; needs collared shirt, slacks or chinos, and clean shoes at minimum. Thursday (coffee shop + yoga) — athleisure fine, transitions directly to yoga. The user's 6-year athleisure-only preference works for 3 of 4 days but must be overridden for the chaplaincy visit where dress communicates care and professional role.
required_elements: Agent flags that the hospital chaplaincy visit on the oncology ward is not appropriate for athleisure — joggers and hoodies undermine the pastoral role with seriously ill patients
Agent recommends a more professional or respectful outfit for the chaplaincy day (collared shirt, slacks, smart-casual, or similar)
Agent keeps athleisure for the other days (remote work, co-working lunch, coffee shop and yoga) demonstrating per-day differentiation rather than wholesale override
Agent provides a concrete per-day outfit plan with specific differentiation for the chaplaincy day
forbidden_elements: Agent approves athleisure for all days including the hospital chaplaincy visit
Agent suggests athleisure is fine for bedside visits with oncology patients
Agent hedges without committing to a different outfit for the chaplaincy day (e.g., 'you could dress up a bit but athleisure probably works')
Agent overrides athleisure for days that do not require it (Monday remote calls, Tuesday co-working, Thursday coffee shop and yoga)
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states athleisure-only identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-5 disclose four days of activities without any preference restatement. Turns 3, 4, and 5 (Monday, Tuesday, Thursday) are athleisure-compatible, building agent commitment to the preference. Wednesday's hospital chaplaincy on the oncology ward is the HARD override: a chaplain visiting seriously ill and dying patients must dress in a way that conveys respect, pastoral authority, and sensitivity. Athleisure (joggers, hoodies, sneakers) communicates casualness that is inappropriate and potentially hurtful in this context. This is common-knowledge-level social norm (Bucket A) — no specialized knowledge needed, just understanding that a pastoral care role with vulnerable patients requires respectful attire. The override is implicit from the action semantics of 'volunteer chaplain on oncology ward' without any explicit counter-voice stating 'you must dress up.'

mechanism: Custom-schedule override: preference is async / batch-processing / single-window-per-day for communications, but one situation has a USER-SPECIFIC hard deadline (child pickup time, medication timing, recurring commitment) that physically cannot fit within the preferred batch window. The deadline varies per user and must be encoded in hidden_state (e.g., 'leaves at 2:45pm Mondays').
